# PngSuite corpus

Vendored copy of Willem van Schaik's PngSuite, the standard PNG-decoder
conformance test set.

- **Source**: `http://www.schaik.com/pngsuite2011/PngSuite-2017jul19.tgz`
- **Downloaded**: 2026-07-11
- **License**: `PngSuite.LICENSE` (freeware; see file) — original files
  unmodified, vendored verbatim.
- **Original readme**: `PngSuite.README`

## Contents

175 individual `*.png` test files plus `PngSuite.png` (the suite's logo
image, harmless extra coverage) — 176 PNGs total, unmodified from the
archive.

## Corrupt files

Files named `x*.png` are PngSuite's intentionally corrupt/erroneous test
files (bad CRCs, truncated chunks, invalid structure, …) — see
`CORRUPT.txt` (generated by `tests/py/pngsuite_truth.py`) for the exact
list. These get **no** pixel truth in `tests/corpus/pngsuite-truth/`;
PILean's PNG decoder must reject each with a `DecodeError`, never panic or
hang, regardless of whether a lenient decoder (Pillow included, for one of
the fourteen) happens to open it anyway.

## Pixel truth

`tests/corpus/pngsuite-truth/<name>.praw` holds the Pillow-decoded pixel
truth for every non-corrupt file, generated by
`python3 tests/py/pngsuite_truth.py` (invoked automatically by
`gen_golden.py`). See that script's module docstring for PILean's exact
"v1 normalization" rules (8-bit truncation of 16-bit samples, tRNS folded
into the palette, etc.) — a full crosscheck run compares PILean's own PNG
decoder output against these same fixtures.
